Title:
Can't correctly mount SD card on a PX4 (V1) setup

Description:
The current master (flashed via QGC but also locally built) on a V1 setup will show the microSD card as mounted but no files are visible. Stable works fine. The issue does not effect Pixhawks (V2).

Comments:
- Thanks for the report! Could you revert this diff and let us know if that changes anything? ```diff @@ -417,7 +417,7 @@ CONFIG_PREALLOC_TIMERS=50 # Stack and heap information # CONFIG_IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE=3500 -CONFIG_USERMAIN_STACKSIZE=3000 +CONFIG_USERMAIN_STACKSIZE=2600 CONFIG_PTHREAD_STACK_MIN=512 CONFIG_PTHREAD_STACK_DEFAULT=2048 @@ -719,11 +719,11 @@ CONFIG_SCHED_WORKQUEUE=y CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK=y CONFIG_SCHED_WORKPRIORITY=192 CONFIG_SCHED_WORKPERIOD=5000 -CONFIG_SCHED_WORKSTACKSIZE=2048 +CONFIG_SCHED_WORKSTACKSIZE=1800 CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK=y CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY=50 CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPERIOD=50000 -CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKSTACKSIZE=2048 +CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKSTACKSIZE=1800 # CONFIG_LIB_KBDCODEC is not set # CONFIG_LIB_SLCDCODEC is not set ```
- Other than that a GIT bisect between master and stable would be great. I tried to linearize our history in the last weeks, so it should be a bit easier than previously.
- @username_0 Since you fixed the landing detector I presume you somehow were able to boot - what is the status of this issue?
- This isn't fixed yet. I can't sit down for very long at one time at the moment but what I think is happening is there seems to be an issue with flashing updates to the PX4IO somehow. At one point I noticed the firmware update tone started and was overridden by something else. Now I can reproduce the failure by flashing a local vs continuous build one and microsd access isn't working until I force an IO flash (power on with safety button held down). Of course this might just be introducing a delay and isn't directly related. Still looking when I get free blocks of time. Up next, hook up the debug cable.
- @username_2 Sounds like we have the timing related issue on the IO upgrade now also on master, not just nuttx_bringup. @username_0 I suspect a timing fail because the boot process is now faster, as we made the stack checking a debug option. Inspecting and fixing this is lined up.
- @username_0 When you are unable to run ls, what does ```free``` tell you? I expect some sort of secondary dependency due to not enough memory or similar.
- Memory is fine (32k free). Let me check again with the land_detector fix branch vs current master via QGC to make sure the missing land_detector isn't having a strange effect...even though it's started much later than the mounting of the sd card.
- Nope. So one of two things happen: either I can't cd to the microsd directory or I can and it appears to be empty. Timing: can I add a delay somewhere to verify this?
- I just built and installed master on px4fmu-v2 and the pio FW upgrade works from boot with pio running or boot with pio running the bootloader. Is this only on v1?
- Yep. V2 is fine. It's only V1. I probably should try with a second V1 just to be sure.
- Is one of the symptoms that the fmu try to reprogram the pio on every reset or power on?
- I don't think it is trying to everytime. The startup sequence below doesn't try to program it. Interesting is through that after mounting the microsd there are some ops (ie: dataman) that appear to succeed but once booting is complete the microsd isn't available. ``` [boot] Successfully initialized SPI port 1 [boot] Enabling IN12/13 instead of SPI2 [boot] Initializing SPI port 3 [boot] Successfully initialized SPI port 3 [boot] Successfully bound SPI port 3 to the MMCSD driver [i] Looking for microSD... Seemed to be related to the flashed px4io firmware at the time. Or an alternative approach?
- No, it should not, as we have no resources to keep it enabled. There are two potential explanations: a) The stack checking wasn't fully disabled. But I did check in the completely compile output of all configs that it in fact is. And b) there was a race condition present for the whole time, which is now exposed. @username_2 Do you have FMUv1 hardware? If not, could you ask 3DR to ship you some?

My proposal would be re-enabling the stack check in master now until NuttX 7 is ready as master is currently broken for FMUV1 hardware.

- @username_0 Did the memcpy fix that is currently on master and nuttx_bringup fix this issue on V1 HW (with stack checking off)?
- I'll re - test this morning and let you know.
- This is still an issue on the current master. Flashing and then trying to access /fs/microsd fails. I'm have issue building nuttx_bringup this time so I can't yet verify if this fixes it or not. @username_2 did you receive a V1 setup?
- Yes. I did. This may be related to a bug clobbering the heap. I am looking at now. If I can get to this today. I will, if not it will be beginning of next week
- Potentially fixed here: https://github.com/PX4/NuttX/commits/master
- A test with the latest master works :) I tried powering via USB as well as battery which according to one user caused different results. Thanks!

Title:
Cannot open shell on pod on Linux (chdir failed)

Description:
**Describe the bug** After deploying a k3d cluster on a remote Raspberry Pi, the Linux Lens application is not able to open a shell on pods, failing with `chdir(2) failed.: No such file or directory`. The Mac Intel Lens application has not such problem. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Deploy a k3d cluster on a remote server 2. Connect Lens to the cluster 3. Title: CI: K8sServicesTest Checks service across nodes Tests NodePort BPF BPF NAT engine handles unknown protocol packets Should not drop SCTP packets Description: In https://jenkins.cilium.io/job/Cilium-PR-K8s-1.20-kernel-4.19/918/testReport/junit/Suite-k8s-1/20/K8sServicesTest_Checks_service_across_nodes_Tests_NodePort_BPF_BPF_NAT_engine_handles_unknown_protocol_packets_Should_not_drop_SCTP_packets/: ``` /home/jenkins/workspace/Cilium-PR-K8s-1.20-kernel-4.19/src/github.com/cilium/cilium/test/ginkgo-ext/scopes.go:518 Expected : 0 to be > : 0 /home/jenkins/workspace/Cilium-PR-K8s-1.20-kernel-4.19/src/github.com/cilium/cilium/test/k8sT/Services.go:1393 ``` The problem here is that iperf transmits no data (0 bytes), which is not greater than 0. Test output (stderr) shows that iperf3 fails with an error: ``` iperf3: error - control socket has closed unexpectedly command terminated with exit code 1 ``` [e3cb6a69_K8sServicesTest_Checks_service_across_nodes_Tests_NodePort_BPF_BPF_NAT_engine_handles_unknown_protocol_packets_Should_not_drop_SCTP_packets (1).zip](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/files/6789208/e3cb6a69_K8sServicesTest_Checks_service_across_nodes_Tests_NodePort_BPF_BPF_NAT_engine_handles_unknown_protocol_packets_Should_not_drop_SCTP_packets.1.zip) Comments: - ### Initial Analysis `iperf3-server-9pf5x`, the source pod is on k8s2, with IP address 192.168.36.12. It's trying to reach 192.168.36.11 so we don't have any visibility on that traffic (BPF programs are attached on native devices but monitor aggregation is enabled so no `{to,from}-network` traces).
According to `test-output.log`, the iperf3 client failed with: ``` iperf3: error - control socket has closed unexpectedly ``` The server failed with: ``` iperf3: error - unable to read from stream socket: Bad file descriptor ``` [Many reports](https://github.com/esnet/iperf/issues/620) of this error on the iperf repository, so probably fairly generic. ### CI Dashboard Analysis Via the [CI Dashboard](https://datastudio.google.com/s/l4cvgJkTZ9c), I found one other case on master, dating from June 30th: https://jenkins.cilium.io/job/cilium-master-k8s-1.16-kernel-net-next/549/testReport/junit/Suite-k8s-1/16/K8sServicesTest_Checks_service_across_nodes_Tests_NodePort_BPF_BPF_NAT_engine_handles_unknown_protocol_packets_Should_not_drop_SCTP_packets/ [20394869_K8sServicesTest_Checks_service_across_nodes_Tests_NodePort_BPF_BPF_NAT_engine_handles_unknown_protocol_packets_Should_not_drop_SCTP_packets.zip](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/files/6789490/20394869_K8sServicesTest_Checks_service_across_nodes_Tests_NodePort_BPF_BPF_NAT_engine_handles_unknown_protocol_packets_Should_not_drop_SCTP_packets.zip) ### Next Steps We are missing the SCTP `ss` output to be able to check the listening/established connections. I'll send a PR to fix that. We can also temporarily disable monitor aggregation for that test.

Title:
[bug] Timeouts uploading large packages to Artifactory

Description:
Not sure what specifically causes it, but would love to know if possible, and if so how to work around the problem. On the client side, it seems like the upload completes, then 3 minutes later the request times out: ``` 2022-03-28T18:20:45.5757918Z Uploading package 1/1: c37b72a856a3a472e507edcc5b9e7a477dd0c3a9 to '***redacted***' [0m 2022-03-28T18:20:45.5946725Z ... 2022-03-28T18:31:53.9083875Z Uploading conan_package.tgz : 99%|#########9| 3.77G/3.79G [01:04<00:00, 92.0MB/s] 2022-03-28T18:31:54.0079369Z Uploading conan_package.tgz : 99%|#########9| 3.77G/3.79G [01:04<00:00, 93.1MB/s] 2022-03-28T18:31:54.1162492Z Uploading conan_package.tgz : 100%|#########9| 3.78G/3.79G [01:04<00:00, 98.7MB/s] 2022-03-28T18:31:54.1164185Z Uploading conan_package.tgz : 100%|#########9| 3.79G/3.79G [01:04<00:00, 96.4MB/s] 2022-03-28T18:31:54.1164743Z 2022-03-28T18:31:54.1166293Z 2022-03-28T18:31:54.1167084Z Uploaded conan_package.tgz -> Installer/220328.4216+ee6a6afb@ci/branch_releases_22.03.28:c37b [3978144.30k] 2022-03-28T18:34:54.4232074Z [1m[31mERROR: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='conan.ci.eng.***redacted***.com', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /artifactory/api/conan/conan-local/v1/files/***redacted***/Installer/220328.4216+ee6a6afb/branch_releases_22.03.28/0/package/c37b72a856a3a472e507edcc5b9e7a477dd0c3a9/0/conan_package.tgz (Caused by ReadTimeoutError("HTTPSConnectionPool(host='conan.ci.eng.***redacted***.com', port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=60.0)",))[0m ``` On the Artifactory side: ``` 2022-03-28 18:31:54,129 [http-nio-8081-exec-9] [INFO ] (o.a.e.UploadServiceImpl:399) - Deploy to 'conan-local:redacted/Installer/220328.4216+ee6a6afb/branch_releases_22.03.28/0/package/c37b72a856a3a472e507edcc5b9e7a477dd0c3a9/0/conan_package.tgz' Content-Length: 4073619764 2022-03-28 18:32:54,836 [http-nio-8081-exec-9] [ERROR] (o.a.a.c.r.ArtifactoryService:542) - Failed to read stream: java.io.EOFException: Unexpected EOF read on the socket org.jfrog.storage.binstore.ifc.ClientInputStreamException: Failed to read stream: java.io.EOFException: Unexpected EOF read on the socket at org.jfrog.storage.binstore.ifc.ClientStream.read(ClientStream.java:36) at org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils.copyLarge(IOUtils.java:1158) at org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils.copy(IOUtils.java:878) at org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils.copyLarge(IOUtils.java:1135) ``` Note the timestamps: the upload completes at 18:31:54 from the client side, and `Deploy` action on the server side begins at the same time. The server then errors out a minute later, with the client sitting for another 2 minutes before seeing an error. This seems to only happen with very large packages, and only in about 70-80% of the cases (e.g. if we retry enough times it will succeed). How can it be fixed?

Comments:
- I can see that perhaps the fronting nginx's timeout is too small now? ``` location / { client_max_body_size 4000m; client_body_timeout 1800s; # Default is 60, May need to be increased for very large uploads try_files $uri @conan; } ```
- I would recommend trying a couple of things: - To run the same, same package, against a local Artifactory instance (you can easily grab an ArtifactoryCE) running in the same computer. Trying to rule out possible client side issues. - Try and report the same upload in different platforms Linux, Windows, Mac. Does it happens in all of them? More or less with same frequency? - If you are not managing the Artifactory, talk to the team maintaining it. It could have some configuration on the server side, or in the front (Nginx or whatever) that could limit some resource, size, memory bandwidth, or something like that
- What does the `Deploy` stage do? Does it simply copy the resulting package, or is there a more elaborate processing, that involves uncompressing and reading the contents? I wonder if something like this happens: - package uploads, but the HTTP request is still outstanding, sitting idle, waiting for server response - server receives the archive, but takes > 60s to process it - the client, after sitting idle for 60s gives up, and drops the connection - the server treats it as client-side error Pure conjecture (I haven't looked at the code), but given the timing of log messages seems possible?
- Up to my knowledge the Deploy stage should be relatively cheap. The compressed uploaded files don't need to be read at all, because the information that is needed goes in the uncompressed conaninfo.txt, and that is easy and fast to parse. But I am not an Artifactory expert. If you are JFrog customers, I'd suggest filing a support ticket directly against Artifactory. Some of the above suggestion would help in anyway to discard those things. In a local instance you should be able to see the Deploy time too and see if it is relevant or not.

Summary:
GraphQL query error responses do not conform to GraphQL specification

Description:
*Problem:* Currently, the {{DefaultQueryExecutor.execute}} method does not let GraphQL query execution errors pass on to {{result}}. After executing GraphQL query, any errors are accumulated as strings and wrapped into an exception [0]. This causes errors to be omitted from GraphQL response, as the result is never returned [1]. As a consequence, The GraphQL client receives a cryptic error response, which is - not conformed to GraphQL specs - not useful, as it does not give a hint what actually went wrong *Proposed solution:* An exception in such a case should not be thrown, rather errors should be returned as part of the GraphQL result, conforming to GraphQL specs [2]. *Example:* {code:java} Query { articles { items { _path author_DOES_NOT_EXIST } } } {code} (Note: author_DOES_NOT_EXIST field name is intentionally wrong.) *Current response:* {code:java} { "message": "Failed to execute 'text' on 'Response': body stream already read", "stack": "TypeError: Failed to execute 'text' on 'Response': body stream already read\n at https://<host-url>/graphiql.html:64:29" } {code} *Expected response:* {code:java} { "errors": [ { "message": "Validation error of type FieldUndefined: Field 'author_DOES_NOT_EXIST' in type 'ArticleModel' is undefined @ 'articles/items/author_DOES_NOT_EXIST'", "locations": [ { "line": 5, "column": 7 } ], "extensions": { "classification": "ValidationError" } } ] } {code} Which is more meaningful, and conformed to GraphQL errors scpecification [2]. It appears to be a race condition where the the server immediately responds to the IPERF_DONE with a TCP FIN, but the client TCP has not yet sent the FIN. As a solution, would it be a good idea to add a sleep in the server(iperf_run_server() function) after it exits the main loop when test_state is set to IPERF_DONE, and before the cleanup_server() is called? ` if (result == 0 || (timeout != NULL && timeout->tv_sec == 0 && timeout->tv_usec == 0)) { /* Run the timers. */ (void) gettimeofday(&now, NULL); tmr_run(&now); } } sleep(2); cleanup_server(test); `

- Problem: you have 64-bit Python, and a 32-bit installer. This will cause problems for extension modules. The reasons why the installer doesn't finds Python is the transparent 32-bit emulation from Windows 7. 64-bit and 32-bit programs will write to different parts of the Windows registry. 64-bit: HKLM|HKCU\SOFTWARE\ 32-bit: HKLM|HKCU\SOFTWARE\wow6432node\ . This means that the 64-bit Python installer writes to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Python , but the 32-bit setuptools installer looks at HKLM\SOFTWARE\wow6432node\Python (this is handled by windows automatically, programs don't notice). This is expected behavior and not a bug. Usually, you have these choices: the "clean" way: use 32-bit Python if you have to use 32-bit modules or extensions the other "clean" way: only use 64-bit installers when using 64-bit Python (see below) what the answer above suggests: copy HKLM\SOFTWARE\Python to HKLM\SOFTWARE\wow6432node\Python , but this will cause problems with binary distributions, as 64-bit Python can't load 32-bit compiled modules (do NOT do this!) install pure Python modules with setuptools instead of the distutils installer (easy_install or pip) For setuptools itself, for example, you can't use a 32-bit installer for 64-bit Python as it includes binary files. But there's a 64-bit installer at http://www.lfd.uci.edu/~gohlke/pythonlibs/ (has many installers for other modules too) . Nowadays, many packages on PyPi have binary distributions, so you can install them via pip.
- For 64-bit Python on Windows download ez_setup.py and run it; it will download the appropriate .egg file and install it for you. At the time of writing the .exe installer does not support 64-bit versions of Python for Windows, due to a distutils installer compatibility issue .
- I made a registry (.reg) file that will automatically change the registry for you. It works if it's installed in "C:\Python27": Download 32-bit version HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE|HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\wow6432node\ Download 64-bit version HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE|HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\
- Yes, you are correct, the issue is with 64-bit Python and 32-bit installer for setuptools. The best way to get 64-bit setuptools installed on Windows is to download ez_setup.py to C:\Python27\Scripts and run it. It will download appropriate 64-bit .egg file for setuptools and install it for you. Source: http://pypi.python.org/pypi/setuptools P.S. I'd recommend against using 3rd party 64-bit .exe setuptools installers or manipulating registry
- Create a file named python2.7.reg (registry file) and put this content into it: Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00 [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Python\PythonCore\2.7] [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Python\PythonCore\2.7\Help] [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Python\PythonCore\2.7\Help\MainPythonDocumentation] @="C:\\Python27\\Doc\\python26.chm" [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Python\PythonCore\2.7\InstallPath] @="C:\\Python27\\" [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Python\PythonCore\2.7\InstallPath\InstallGroup] @="Python 2.7" [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Python\PythonCore\2.7\Modules] [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Python\PythonCore\2.7\PythonPath] @="C:\\Python27\\Lib;C:\\Python27\\DLLs;C:\\Python27\\Lib\\lib-tk" And make sure every path is right! Title:

Description:
`pqos -sv` reports "contention bit-mask": ``` ... INFO: L3 CAT details: CDP support=1, CDP on=0, #COS=16, #ways=11, ways contention bit-mask 0x600 ... ``` `rdtset` warns about "contention mask", e.g.: ``` $ sudo rdtset -r 0 -t 'l3=0x7f;cpu=2,4,6,8,10' -t 'l3=0x780;cpu=0,12,14' -c 2 sleep 1000 CAT: One or more of requested L3 CBMs (MASK: 0x780) overlap contention mask. ``` Architecturally and performance-wise, what does "contention bit-mask" really mean? The default mask on my Xeon Gold 6250 is 0x7ff so I understand there are 11 ways. Does the contention mask of 0x600 mean that the upper 2 ways are somehow special? Special in what way? Why does rdtset warn me when the mask I provide overlaps the contention mask? Should I avoid using the upper 2 ways when giving masks to rdtset?

Comments:
- Hi, The contention bit mask is shared by CPU cores and other entities (e.g IO device such as PCIe, CXL, etc... ). Yes, you are right the upper 2 ways of 0x7ff are the contention mask. rdtset warns because depending on the application type, overlapping with these may impact your application performance. You can also see this https://github.com/intel/intel-cmt-cat/issues/135 Thanks, Khawar

Title:
__getattr__ doesn't work with __enter__ -> AttributeError

Description:
I would like to use with on an object that uses __getattr__ to redirect calls. Howerver, this does not seem to work with the method __enter__ Please consider the following, simplified code to reproduce the error: class EnterTest(object): def myenter(self): pass def __exit__(self, type, value, traceback): pass def __getattr__(self, name): if name == '__enter__': return self.myenter enter_obj = EnterTest() print getattr(enter_obj, '__enter__') with enter_obj: pass Output: <bound method EnterTest.myenter of <__main__.EnterTest object at 0x00000000021432E8>> Traceback (most recent call last): File "test.py", line 14, in <module> with enter_obj: AttributeError: __enter__ Why doesn't it fall back to __getattr__ since __enter__ does not exist on the object? Of course, I could make it work if I just create an __enter__ method and redirect from there instead, but I'm wondering why it doesn't work otherwise. My python version is the following: C:\Python27\python27.exe 2.7 (r27:82525, Jul 4 2010, 07:43:08) [MSC v.1500 64 bit (AMD64)]

Answers:
- According to upstream, this working was a bug in 2.6 which was "fixed" in 2.7. The short answer is that methods like __enter__ are looked up on the class, not on the object. The documentation for this obscure behavior is at http://docs.python.org/reference/datamodel#specialnames : x[i] is roughly equivalent to ... type(x).__getitem__(x, i) for new-style classes . You can see this behavior with other special methods: class foo(object): def __iadd__(self, i): print i a = foo() a += 1 class foo2(object): def __getattr__(self, key): print key raise AttributeError b = foo2() b += 1 class foo3(object): pass def func(self, i): print i c = foo3() c.__iadd__ = func c += 1 The first works; the second two don't. Python 2.6 didn't conform to this behavior for __enter__ and __exit__ , but 2.7 does. http://bugs.python.org/issue9259 That said, it's painfully inconsistent that these methods can't be handled dynamically like any other attributes can. Similarly, you can't instrument accesses to these methods with __getattribute__ like you can any other method. I can't find any intrinsic design logic to this. Python is normally very consistent, and this is a fairly unpleasant wart.

- This is your current error: ```C++ include/min.hpp:47:38: error: static assertion failed: min(A, B): Cannot compare types A and B ``` The ```is_comparable``` check is defined as: ```C++ template <typename A, typename B> struct is_comparable { enum { value = std::is_same<A, B>::value || ( std::is_integral<A>::value && std::is_integral<B>::value && sizeof(A) >= sizeof(B)) }; }; ``` Primecount uses the nonstandard ```__int128_t``` type which is not supported default by the ```std::is_integral``` trait if I remember correctly. Therefore primecount must be compiled using the ```-std=gnu++11``` (or -std=gnu++14, -std=gnu++17) (when using GCC or Clang) which is usually enabled by default. My guess is that in your build you use e.g. ```-std=c++11``` instead?! Another reason that could explain your build issue is that your compiler is too old and that its ```std::is_integral``` implementation does not work correctly for ```__int128_t``` even with ```-std=gnu++11```.
- Primecount used to have the following workaround for this issue (https://github.com/username_1/primecount/blob/v5.3/include/int128_t.hpp#L147): ```C++ template <typename T> struct is_integral { enum { #if !defined(HAVE_INT128_T) value = std::is_integral<T>::value #else value = std::is_integral<T>::value || std::is_same<T, int128_t>::value || std::is_same<T, uint128_t>::value #endif }; }; ``` I removed this workaround some time ago when both GCC and Clang's ```std::is_integral``` implementation correctly worked with ```int128_t``` by default (with ```-std=gnu++11``` or ```-std=gnu++14```).

- This seems like a good idea, however I was unable to implement this idea cleanly in CMake. Ideally the GNU extensions should be enabled if the C++ compiler uses the GNU dialect. CMake supports ```CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS``` however this option only works (in my tests) if the C++ version is hardcoded to a specific version (see last code section) which is not ideal for primecount (as primecount uses recent C++ features if the preprocessor detects that the compiler supports it). I tried adding the following code to primecount's ```CMakeLists.txt``` but it has no effect: ```CMake # Does not work if compiled with: # cmake . -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-std=c++17" if (CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_FRONTEND_VARIANT STREQUAL "GNU") set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS ON) endif() ``` Is it possible to change your build system script to compile primecount with ```-std=gnu++17``` instead of ```-std=c++17``` or add ```-std=gnu++17``` after ```-std=c++17``` when building for conda (e.g. try ```cmake . -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-std=gnu++17"```)? Alternatively you could also patch primecount's ```CMakeLists.txt``` using: ```CMake # Works correctly if compiled with: # cmake . -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-std=c++17" # Compiler flags will be: "-std=c++17 -std=gnu++11 ..." if (CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_FRONTEND_VARIANT STREQUAL "GNU") set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11) set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS ON) endif() ``` I don't want to add this workaround to primecount as this hardcodes the C++ version which is not ideal. I am open to other suggestions but so far I am not aware of any clean solution that would fix this issue.
- Perhaps @username_2 can help
- We prefer not to add such workarounds for broken upstream build systems
- Of all the workaround discussed so far the ```is_integral``` workaround https://github.com/username_1/primecount/pull/52#issuecomment-998555388 seems to be the best solution so far. This workaround will likely make primecount compatible with the ```-std=c++*``` compiler option. I am willing to add this workaround to primecount (if this is useful to sagemath), however I would prefer not to do an immediate release just because of this issue. Would this still be helpful to sagemath?
- Yes, this would still be helpful, as we can easily add upstream commits as patches to sagemath.
- Unfortunately the ```is_integral``` workaround I intended to implement has turned out much more complicated than expected. When using GCC & Clang the C++ standard library does not support 128-bit integers if the flag ```-std=c++*``` is used (this option disables the GNU extensions that are otherwise enabled by default). I have identified at least 5 functions (```std::numeric_limits```, ```std::is_integral```, ```std::is_signed```, ```std::is_unsigned```, ```std::make_unsigned```) that do not work with ```-std=c++*```. Those functions are used all over the place in primecount's code base and would require hundreds of code lines to be modified. It is also a minefield, I cannot rule out that there are other STL functions that do not work either for 128-bit integers and ```-std=c++*```. Therefore I have decided not to implement this workaround. The other option to fix this issue in primecount would have been to force enabling the GNU extensions in primecount's build system even if the user tries to disable the GNU extensions using the ```-std=c++*``` option. Unfortunately GCC/Clang do not have a ```--gnu-extensions``` flag and CMake's ```CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS``` only works if the C++ version is hardcoded (which is generally a bad idea and in primecount's case will generate suboptimal code as features from recent C++ versions won't be used). **Hence I have given up and primecount simply cannot be compiled with ```-std=c++*``` (because this disables the GNU extensions which primecount requires for 128-bit integers) and you should use ```-std=gnu++*``` instead** (or use neither ```-std=c++*``` nor ```-std=gnu++*``` in which case ```-std=gnu++*``` will be used by default). I have looked up [conda's build system code](https://github.com/conda/conda-build/blob/0a6efdcfa02484954e7a3fdf5c2ec4bb3cb6682e/conda_build/jinja_context.py#L416) and found the following comment: ```Python "compilerflags": { # When put into a CDT these should be the base defaults. # Package builds can and will change these frequently. "CPPFLAGS": "-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2", "CFLAGS": "-march=nocona -mtune=haswell -ftree-vectorize -fPIC -fstack-protector-strong -O2 -pipe", "CXXFLAGS": "-fvisibility-inlines-hidden -std=c++17 -fmessage-length=0 -march=nocona -mtune=haswell -ftree-vectorize -fPIC -fstack-protector-strong -O2 -pipe", ... ``` So it seems to me that it is possible to change the ```CXXFLAGS``` when building a package/library for conda and that changing the compiler options for specific packages even happens frequently. Hence I suggest for the primecount conda build to modify the ```CXXFLAGS``` flags to e.g. ```CXXFLAGS="${CXXFLAGS} -std=gnu++17"``` which will overwrite the unsupported default ```-std=c++17``` option. Here is a [blog post](http://www.johnlees.me/blog/2018/10/15/creating-a-conda-package-with-compilation-and-dependencies/) where somebody modified the ```CXXFLAGS``` the same way for building the Boost library for conda. (Another option which has the same effect is to compile primecount for conda using: ```cmake . -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -std=gnu++17"```)
- Using `-std=gnu++17` for a library implies the same for a Python extension which uses it - and, for primecount deps, namely primesieve. So this build change is not very local. AFAIK, boost has multiprecision ints - although yes, I'd fully understand that adding boost as a dependency for primecount is not much fun...
- This means that users cannot install primecount from source out of the box in a conda environment.
- We are not in the business of building a conda package. We are trying to build `primecount` in the role of a user *in* a conda environment.
- I am sorry, but in order to safely support the ```-std=c++*``` option in primecount I would have to reimplement the entire C++ standard library with support for 128-bit integers. This is unfeasible. I have also read the GCC source code to find if I can abuse some macro to force enabling 128-bit integer support in the STL, but I could not find any. If you really need to be able to compile primecount with ```-std=c++*``` then 128-bit integer support must be disabled in primecount. For GCC & Clang this can be achieved using (I have tested this, all tests passed successfully): ``` cmake .. -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-U__SIZEOF_INT128__" ```
- I think this would make sense.
- I have now implemented this feature, I think this feature will provide value to other users as well. The CMake configure step now checks if the C++ compiler and the C++ standard library support 128-bit integers. If not, support 128-bit integers will be disabled automatically. If the user has specified the ```-std=c++*``` command-line option then a warning message will be displayed which explains that 128-bit integer support has been disabled because of this flag: ```bash $ CXXFLAGS="-std=c++17" cmake .. -- The CXX compiler identification is GNU 11.2.0 -- Detecting CXX compiler ABI info -- Detecting CXX compiler ABI info - done -- Check for working CXX compiler: C:/msys64/mingw64/bin/c++.exe - skipped -- Detecting CXX compile features -- Detecting CXX compile features - done -- Performing Test int128 -- Performing Test int128 - Failed -- Performing Test int128_with_cpp11 -- Performing Test int128_with_cpp11 - Failed CMake Warning at CMakeLists.txt:196 (message): Your usage of -std=c++* disables 128-bit integer support in primecount, primecount will only support numbers <= 2^63. Title:
Google Pixel C Keyboard Escape key handling

Description:
Hi, I have recently (naturally) aquired a Pixel C with the Pixel C Keyboard. Almost everything seems to be working, there is just an annoyance preventing me from using termux fully. Since they Pixel C Keyboard is missing keys, there are build-in [hotkeys](https://support.google.com/pixel/answer/6326992?hl=en) for the missing ones. However: If I press the ![...](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/FS30qf3hlMsphqXMswSDwRgvOnHTBOG0Tnip2Gb5hnNOvW6VkKf8u6jL1zJBmMG8vvJi=w18-rwa)+1 key that maps to escape I *also* get the extended-keys soft-keyboard. It makes vi quite frustrating to use :) I believe this is an issue with termux because: - other programs I tried to not have this behaviour - termux does not have this behavour with other keys like [ or ] that are also not present as physical keys. - escape keys are funny with terminals :)

Comments:
- With '_get the extended-keys soft-keyboard_', do you mean that the soft keyboard pops up in addition to the escape key being sent?
- Correct. There is some coupling between the hardware and the software keyboard. The 'search', 'alt' and '...' key are all used as regular modifier keys, but they also have their own function if not used as a modifier. Similar to how windows treats the 'windows' (aka 'meta'?) key: win+key is an action, but just the win key also pops up the start menu. In the case of the Pixel C Keyboard the ... functions like AltGr does when you have a non-English keyboard layout selected, so perhaps it really just *is* that key (e.g.: if you select Us-International layout, the '...'+5 turns into a €). If you however just press that key, you get the soft-keyboard extended symbols tab. Just like if just press the 'alt' key, you get the soft-keyboard emoji tab. The escape key seems to be treated differently than other keys in this manner. '...'+o and '...'+p just insert the correct [ and ] key. '...'+1 correctly functions like escape, but also still opens the soft-keyboard as if you did not press the 1 key before releasing the '...' key. If I were to guess, perhaps only the '1' key is marked as consumed but the '...' modifier key is not? Perhaps the keyboard literally sends AltGr-down, Esc-down, Esc-up, AltGr-up, and termux doesn't eat the modifier key for escape like it does for other keys, so it arrives at the system which only sees the AltGr events and does the soft-keyboard stuff.
- Perhaps it has to do with ["replace" key event] support, apparently new in android, see: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/a43a96b%5E%21/#F0 where they added the mapping for the <AltR>+1 -> ESCAPE to the keyboard driver. This is really a special beast it seems?
- @username_0 Could you use the app https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sonelli.keywatcher and press ...+1 (which I understand should result in just the Escape key being executed by Termux, and nothing more, right?) and attach the output here (or mail it to me)?
- I did some playing around with the app. My observations: * flags, source, keyboard type and device id are constant * the ...+1 -> esc mapping IS special * the ...+2 0-> ` mapping is NOT special. * the 1 key has keycode 8 * the 2 key has keycode 9 * the key with ...+1 has keycode 111 (this is esc?) * the key with ...+2 still has keycode 9 Logging follows: ### Pressing '...'+'1': Date: Wed Dec 23 19:21:37 GMT+01:00 2015 Device Manufacturer: google Device Model: Pixel C Device Board: dragon Device Bootloader: Google_Smaug.7132.260.0 Android Version: REL 6.0.1 (sdk:23) *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 58 Action: 0 Meta State: 34 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 42 *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 111 Action: 0 Meta State: 0 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 42 *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 111 Action: 1 Meta State: 0 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 42 *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 58 Action: 1 Meta State: 0 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 42 ### Pressing just '1' Date: Wed Dec 23 19:33:30 GMT+01:00 2015 Device Manufacturer: google Device Model: Pixel C Device Board: dragon Device Bootloader: Google_Smaug.7132.260.0 Android Version: REL 6.0.1 (sdk:23) *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 8 Action: 0 Meta State: 0 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 42 *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 8 Action: 1 Meta State: 0 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 42 [Truncated] Device Bootloader: Google_Smaug.7132.260.0 Android Version: REL 6.0.1 (sdk:23) *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 9 Action: 0 Meta State: 0 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 42 *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 9 Action: 1 Meta State: 0 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 42
- From [KeyEvent.java](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base.git/+/master/core/java/android/view/KeyEvent.java): public static final int KEYCODE_ALT_RIGHT = 58; public static final int KEYCODE_ESCAPE = 111; public static final int ACTION_DOWN = 0; public static final int ACTION_UP = 1; public static final int META_ALT_ON = 0x02; public static final int META_ALT_RIGHT_ON = 0x20; So the sequence for ...+1: (1) Key Code: 58, Action: 0, Meta State: 34 (2) Key Code: 111, Action: 0, Meta State: 0 (3) Key Code: 111, Action: 1, Meta State: 0 (4) Key Code: 58, Action: 1, Meta State: 0 would mean (since 34=0x02 + 0x20): (1) AltRight down, meta=ALT_ON | ALT_RIGHT_ON (2) Escape down (3) Escape up (4) AltRight up The special thing that Termux in TerminalView.java does is to catch the Escape key in `onKeyPreIme()`, in order to prevent the escape key being treated as back: @Override public boolean onKeyPreIme(int keyCode, KeyEvent event) { if (LOG_KEY_EVENTS) Log.i(EmulatorDebug.LOG_TAG, "onKeyPreIme(keyCode=" + keyCode + ", event=" + event + ")"); if (keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ESCAPE || (keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK && mOnKeyListener.shouldBackButtonBeMappedToEscape())) { // Handle the escape key ourselves to avoid the system from treating it as back key // and e.g. close keyboard. switch (event.getAction()) { case KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN: return onKeyDown(keyCode, event); case KeyEvent.ACTION_UP: return onKeyUp(keyCode, event); } } return super.onKeyPreIme(keyCode, event); } This would return true since `onKeyDown()` and `onKeyUp()` returns true unless `event.isSystem()`, which is not the case here. So if the above flow does not miss anything, it would mean that the problem is due to `onKeyPreIme()` returning `true` for the `Escape down/up` events.
- Which could perhaps make sense - by eating the key event before the IME sees it, the IME would be left with only seeing the two events: (1) AltRight down, meta=ALT_ON | ALT_RIGHT_ON (4) AltRight up which would be the same as just pressing the `...` key. @username_0: Could you test what pressing and releasing just the `...` key sends?
- Intercepting `keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ESCAPE` in `onKeyPreIme()` may not be necessary, at least not longer. It came from Android 4.4 or earlier, where if I recall correctly this was needed to prevent the system from handling Escape as the back key. This intercepting does not seem to be necessary anymore, since at least on Android 5.1 and 6.0 the Escape key is sent to `onKeyDown` as other keys and can be consumed there, without messing with the IME.
- As expected, just the ... key is just the AltR: Date: Fri Dec 25 00:45:40 GMT+01:00 2015 Device Manufacturer: google Device Model: Pixel C Device Board: dragon Device Bootloader: Google_Smaug.7132.260.0 Android Version: REL 6.0.1 (sdk:23) *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 58 Action: 0 Meta State: 34 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 44 *** Key Event Detected *** Key Code: 58 Action: 1 Meta State: 0 Flags: 8 Source: 257 Keyboard Type: 2 Device ID: 44 (and after I press the button, the software keyboard pops up)
- @username_0 Thanks for all the help! Could you try out the newly released `0.23` version of Termux to see if it fixes the issue :pray: ?
- Problem solved. Awesome, thanks.

Title:
Add EDAC hardware check (ECC memory errors)

Description:
This patch will add a `check_hw_edac` check to verify correctable and uncorrectable ECC errors in memory, as reported by [`edac-utils`](https://github.com/grondo/edac-utils) EDAC is an alternative to MCE checks, with support for older hardware (cf. http://www.mcelog.org/faq.html#13) and could be used on platforms where `mcelog` is not available. ``` # edac-util mc1: csrow1: CPU_SrcID#1_Channel#1_DIMM#0: 31 Corrected Errors # nhc -e check_hw_edac MARK_OFFLINE=0 check_hw_edac: ECC errors detected - 31 corrected memory errors detected (limit of 9). ERROR: nhc: Health check failed: check_hw_edac: ECC errors detected - 31 corrected memory errors detected (limit of 9). ERROR: nhc: Health check failed: check_hw_edac: ECC errors detected - 31 corrected memory errors detected (limit of 9). ``` It is very closely modelled after the `check_hw_mcelog` function, with similar thresholds definitions.

Comments:
- EDAC support is high on our priority list at LANL, so getting this merged is very much on my radar and at the top of my priority list! I want to make sure it gets some bake time in production before putting it into a release, so I'm re-targetting this for 1.4.4, but it will be going in very early in the new year! :-)
- The current edac-utils release 0.16 from RHEL/CentOS 7 contains a bug as documented in https://github.com/grondo/edac-utils/blob/master/NEWS: Version 0.18 (2011-11-09); - Do not print "No errors to report" with edac-util --quiet We get this useless output from the command: # edac-util --quiet edac-util: No errors to report. I have opened a bug report for RHEL 7 requesting an upgrade of edac-utils to version 0.18, see https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1662858 Hopefully this will be useful for NHC when Red Hat implementes the update.
- It turns out that edac-utils is deprecated (though still supported) in RHEL 7, and the hardware checking functionality is replaced by rasdaemon, see https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html/migration_planning_guide/sect-red_hat_enterprise_linux-migration_planning_guide-deprecated_packages The rasdaemon is documented for RHEL 7 in https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html/system_administrators_guide/sec-checking_for_hardware_errors The rasdaemon project page is https://pagure.io/rasdaemon Usage of rasdaemon on RHEL 7 requires a daemon: systemctl start rasdaemon Then you can inquire the daemon by the ras-mc-ctl command. For NHC it may be preferable to use rasdaemon in stead of the deprecated edac-utils or mcelog.

Title:
Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets incorrectly adds a rubocop:todo with --disable-uncorrectable

Description:
When running with `--auto-correct --disable-uncorrectable`, a `rubocop:todo` is unnecessarily added. When running rubocop again, it complains with `Unnecessary disabling of Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets` -------- ## Expected behavior Since `Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets` can be auto fixed, it should not output a todo. ## Actual behavior 1\. Given a file `test.rb`: ```ruby # frozen_string_literal: true puts [ :something ] ``` 2\. When running with the default rubocop config (and no other configs in the parent folder tree), it incorrectly adds a TODO for the second bracket on the line: ``` » rubocop --auto-correct --disable-uncorrectable Inspecting 1 file C Offenses: example.rb:3:9: C: [Corrected] Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets: Do not use space inside array brackets. puts [ :something ] ^ example.rb:3:20: C: [Todo] Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets: Do not use space inside array brackets. puts [ :something ] ^ 1 file inspected, 2 offenses detected, 2 offenses corrected ``` The file then looks like this: ```ruby # frozen_string_literal: true puts [:something] # rubocop:todo Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets ``` 3\. Then running same command again results in more changes because of the unnecessary todo: ``` » rubocop --auto-correct --disable-uncorrectable Inspecting 1 file W Offenses: example.rb:3:19: W: [Corrected] Lint/RedundantCopDisableDirective: Unnecessary disabling of Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets. puts [:something] # rubocop:todo Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 1 file inspected, 1 offense detected, 1 offense corrected ``` Now the file is correct: ```ruby # frozen_string_literal: true puts [:something] ``` ## Steps to reproduce the problem Same as "actual" but I'll outline the simple steps: 1. Given a file `test.rb`: ```ruby # frozen_string_literal: true puts [ :something ] ``` 2. `rubocop --auto-correct --disable-uncorrectable` 3. `rubocop` 4. Observe that `Lint/RedundantCopDisableDirective` is unexpectedly reported ## RuboCop version ``` rubocop -V 1.25.0 (using Parser 3.1.0.0, rubocop-ast 1.15.1, running on ruby 3.1.0 arm64-darwin21) - rubocop-rails 2.13.2 - rubocop-rspec 2.8.0 ```

Comments:
- It looks like this is marking the rightmost space between the square bracket as `todo` because it does not detect that it is autocorrectable. ``` ❯ bundle exec rubocop test.rb Offenses: test.rb:3:7: C: [Correctable] Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets: Do not use space inside array brackets. puts [ :something ] ^ test.rb:3:18: C: Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets: Do not use space inside array brackets. puts [ :something ] ^ 1 file inspected, 2 offenses detected, 1 offense auto-correctable ``` However, the first run of `--auto-correct` fixes the two bracket spacing offenses in one go, but it only reports that it fixed one (the one previously marked [Correctable]): ``` ❯ bundle exec rubocop test.rb --auto-correct test.rb:3:7: C: [Corrected] Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets: Do not use space inside array brackets. puts [ :something ] ^ 1 file inspected, 1 offense detected, 1 offense corrected ``` Not sure if this is a problem with `Layout/SpaceInsideArrayLiteralBrackets` cop itself, or the `--disable-uncorrectable` option.

Description:

Comments:

Title:
Style/WordArray autofix ignores Style/PercentLiteralDelimiters settings.

Description:
I have the following configuration: ```yaml Style/PercentLiteralDelimiters: Description: "Use `%`-literal delimiters consistently" Enabled: true PreferredDelimiters: "%i": "[]" "%r": "{}" "%w": "[]" "%W": "[]" "%x": "[]" Style/WordArray: Description: "Use %w or %W for arrays of words." Enabled: true ``` When I run `rubocop --only Style/WordArray -a` it fixes all occurences of word-arrays to use `%w()` syntax. I would expect it to use the settings of the `PercentLiteralDelimiters` cop and fix word-arrays to use the `%w[]` syntax. My version of rubocop is 0.39.0, which is a latest at this point.

Comments:
- BTW, specifying both makes it do what you want: ```bash test master % ../bin/rubocop --only Style/WordArray,Style/PercentLiteralDelimiters test.rb -a Inspecting 1 file C Offenses: test.rb:1:1: C: [Corrected] %w-literals should be delimited by [ and ]. %w(foo bar baz) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ test.rb:1:1: C: [Corrected] Use %w or %W for an array of words. ['foo', 'bar', 'baz'] ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 1 file inspected, 2 offenses detected, 2 offenses corrected test master % cat test.rb %w[foo bar baz] ``` I suppose the question is: can/should one cop look at another cop's config to determine how to autocorrect?
- We prefer not to create new offenses when auto-correcting, but trying to avoid doing so at all costs is a slippery slope and would vastly complicate RC. I think this is OK as is.
- I agree.

Make `Style/SymbolArray` cop to enable by default

Description:
## Expected behavior ```yaml Style/SymbolArray: Enabled: true ``` ## Actual behavior ```yaml Style/SymbolArray: Enabled: false ``` --------- I think the `Style/SymbolArray` cop should be enabled by default, but the cop is disabled by default. https://github.com/username_1/rubocop/blob/master/config/disabled.yml#L117-L120 https://github.com/username_1/rubocop/commit/40cf6848ffc047358371b0d958511b28fbc67fe9 When the cop was added, `TargetRubyVersion` config does not exist. However currently `TargetRubyVersion` exists, so we can make the cop to enable by default. However, the cop has some problems in order to make to enable by default. Handle `TargetRubyVersion` ---------- I guess the cop does not properly handle `TargetRubyVersion` config. https://github.com/username_1/rubocop/blob/a0f3a8f1223ba8d5b45e1bfbd950ff6f81b275f7/lib/rubocop/cop/style/symbol_array.rb#L27-L38 I think the `validate_config` method is unnecessarily. We should use `minimum_target_ruby_version` instead of `validate_config`. Bug -------- The cop has a bug. For example: `.rubocop.yml` ```yaml Style/SymbolArray: Enabled: true EnforcedStyle: brackets ``` `test.rb` ```ruby %i(a a-b) ``` ```sh $ rubocop --only SmybolArray -a Inspecting 1 file C Offenses: test.rb:1:1: C: [Corrected] Use [] for an array of symbols. %i[a a-b] ^^^^^^^^^ 1 file inspected, 1 offense detected, 1 offense corrected $ cat test.rb [:a, :a-b] ``` The meaning of `%i(a a-b)` and `[:a, :a-b]` is different, but RuboCop add an offense for this code. [Truncated] ```ruby FILTER_METHODS = %i(after_filter append_after_filter append_around_filter append_before_filter around_filter before_filter prepend_after_filter prepend_around_filter prepend_before_filter skip_after_filter skip_around_filter skip_before_filter skip_filter).freeze ``` The first code is auto-corrected to second code. The second code is not readable. We will need to add lien breaks manually to this code. `Style/WordArray` supports line brakes feature, so, we should support the feature for `Style/SymbolArray` as well. ------------------ I'll implement the above features, and I'll make to enable by default the cop when finished.

Comments:
- Fine by me. The reason this cop is not enabled by default is that it was developed when we still supported Ruby 1.9.
- For the record, I disagree. This seems like a strange thing to force on people by default given there is no inherent advantage, and it adds cognitive overload for developers.
- @username_2 I am late but agrees, as a newcomer Ruby is complex enough and I wish this was not enabled by default. Pure preference but the least amount of tokens I have to learn the better, I had to learn what was a Symbol and now rubocop introduces %i on top of it ahah :D
- I just think its purely preferential and is doing nothing to add to code readability and if anything its decreasing it. This should _not_ be enabled by default.
- Thanks for your feedback. RuboCop's default rule is based on the Ruby Style Guide, so if you'd like to change the default, I recommend to open an issue to the style guide (opening an issue to this repository is also ok). https://github.com/rubocop-hq/ruby-style-guide#i By the way, personally I still think this cop should be enabled by default. I agree with the cop does not improve readability. But it improves writability by reducing typing `:` and `,` in my opinion. You can find good examples from this file. https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/blob/7e37a77d40e0cb45625bb72c7af051c6fad6932a/lib/rubocop/ast/node.rb And, I think not all Cops improve readability directly. Readability is important, but RuboCop also focuses on consistency. We can enforce ourselves that we use `%i[]` or `[]` with this cop.
- For anyone here wondering how to disable this madness, here's a snippet copy/paste ready. in your `.rubocop.yml`: ```yaml Style/SymbolArray: Enabled: false ```

Title:
[Corrected] Naming/RescuedExceptionsVariableName: Use e instead of error.

Description:
Ruby 2.7.0 Rubocop 0.80.0 I have some code: ```ruby # frozen_string_literal: true def main raise rescue StandardError => error error = { error_message: error.message } puts error end ``` I run CLI rubocop with argument `--auto-correct`: ```bash $ rubocop --auto-correct main.rb ``` ↓ ``` Inspecting 1 file W Offenses: main.rb:5:25: C: [Corrected] Naming/RescuedExceptionsVariableName: Use e instead of error. rescue StandardError => error ^^^^^ main.rb:6:3: W: Lint/UselessAssignment: Useless assignment to variable - error. error = { ^^^^^ 1 file inspected, 2 offenses detected, 1 offense corrected ``` Rubocop corrected my code, renamed rescued exception variable name from `error` to `e`. But this correcting is changed code logic. Before use Rubocop method `main()` return Hash: `{ error: { error_message: String} }`. After use return `RuntimeError`.

Comments:
- @username_3 what is expected correction here? should it be 1 or 2 **1.** ``` # frozen_string_literal: true def main raise rescue StandardError => error error = { error_message: e.message } puts error end ``` **2.** ``` # frozen_string_literal: true def main raise rescue StandardError => error e = { error_message: e.message } puts e end ```
- I believe you might be looking for a third option: ``` # frozen_string_literal: true def main raise rescue StandardError => e e = { error_message: e.message } puts e end ``` or ``` # frozen_string_literal: true def main raise rescue StandardError => e error = { error_message: e.message } puts error end ```
- I agree with @username_2. Ideally, auto-correction would be expected to change only a variable specified by `rescue =>`.
- I agree that calling a variable by the same name as an exception variable is not very correct. However, I am sure that automatic code correction should not affect the logic of its operation. Since I found a scenario in which the automatic correction changed the logic, I suggest removing the automatic code correction from this cop.
- `Naming/RescuedExceptionsVariableName` should rename the variable correctly, i.e. all occurrences of `error` should be changed to `e`, ideally in the correct scope, or at least in the rescue block.

Title:
Infinite loop correcting Layout/EmptyLinesAroundAccessModifier

Description:
Infinite loop when correcting the following code with the default config: ```ruby class A attr_reader :private def private? private end end ``` I looked in the opened issues, and couldn't find anything related, but hope it's not a duplicate. -------- ## Expected behavior Something reasonable, preferably without spurious spaces around `private` ## Actual behavior ``` ➜ a bundle exec rubocop -c .rubocop.yml -a a.rb Inspecting 1 file C Offenses: a.rb:6:1: C: [Corrected] Layout/EmptyLinesAroundMethodBody: Extra empty line detected at method body beginning. a.rb:6:5: C: [Corrected] Layout/EmptyLinesAroundAccessModifier: Keep a blank line before and after private. private ^^^^^^^ a.rb:8:1: C: [Corrected] Layout/EmptyLinesAroundMethodBody: Extra empty line detected at method body end. 0 files inspected, 3 offenses detected, 3 offenses corrected Infinite loop detected in /private/tmp/a/a.rb. /Users/eugene/.rvm/gems/ruby-2.5.3/bundler/gems/rubocop-f51c53c0be3c/lib/rubocop/runner.rb:268:in `check_for_infinite_loop' ``` ## Steps to reproduce the problem Create Gemfile ```ruby source 'https://rubygems.org' gem "rubocop", github: "rubocop-hq/rubocop" ``` Create a.rb ```ruby class A attr_reader :private def private? private end end ``` Create empty .rubocop.yml ```bash touch .rubocop.yml ``` Run: ```bash bundle && bundle exec rubocop -c .rubocop.yml -a a.rb ``` ## RuboCop version I used the latest master (f51c53c0be3c16b47407c947d85beb3db21e86ac). It's also possible to reproduce on the release version. ``` 0.73.0 (using Parser 2.6.3.0, running on ruby 2.5.3 x86_64-darwin18) ```

Comments:
- I think this is a symptom of the underlying #7212: If `Layout/EmptyLinesAroundAccessModifier` did not detect `private` within the method definition above, there would be no infinite loop.
- I'm facing the same issue with the following code: ``` class A def test return nil if public end def test2; end end ``` However it works fine if I remove the test2 method definition: ``` class A def test return nil if public end end ```

Title:
Newer versions fail to auto correct stdin

Description:
## Expected behavior Older versions (f.i. 0.46) behave as expected: ``` echo 'def a; 3; end' |rubocop _0.46.0_ --auto-correct --stdin - Inspecting 1 file C Offenses: <snip> 1 file inspected, 6 offenses detected, 5 offenses corrected ==================== def a 3 end ``` ## Actual behavior Newer versions fail to do the same: ``` echo 'def a; 3; end' |rubocop _0.49.1_ --auto-correct --stdin - Inspecting 0 files 0 files inspected, no offenses detected ==================== def a; 3; end ``` ## RuboCop version Include the output of `rubocop -V`. Here's an example: ``` $ rubocop -V 0.49.1 (using Parser 2.4.0.0, running on ruby 2.4.0 x86_64-linux) ```

Comments:
- It is `--stdin` option bug. RuboCop does not analyse non-ruby file from v0.48.0. https://github.com/bbatsov/rubocop/pull/3997 `--stdin` option has been broken by this change if the option is not received file name that ends with `.rb`. For example: ```bash $ echo 'def a; 3; end' |rubocop _0.49.1_ --auto-correct --stdin - Inspecting 0 files 0 files inspected, no offenses detected ==================== def a; 3; end $ echo 'def a; 3; end' |rubocop _0.49.1_ --auto-correct --stdin something.rb Inspecting 1 file C Offenses: something.rb:1:1: C: [Corrected] Avoid single-line method definitions. def a; 3; end ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ something.rb:1:6: C: [Corrected] Do not use semicolons to terminate expressions. def a; ^ something.rb:1:7: C: [Corrected] Trailing whitespace detected. def a; ^ something.rb:2:4: C: [Corrected] Do not use semicolons to terminate expressions. 3; ^ something.rb:2:5: C: [Corrected] Trailing whitespace detected. 3; ^ 1 file inspected, 5 offenses detected, 5 offenses corrected ==================== def a 3 end ``` Workaround ==== Add a file name to `--stdin` option.
- Thanks for fixing!

Title:
Auto-correcting with `Style/IfUnlessModifier` and `Style/SoleNestedConditional` breaks code

Description:
`Style/IfUnlessModifier` and `Style/SoleNestedConditional` produce incorrect code when auto-correcting the following code: ```ruby if !error_list.nil? if error_list.first == 'Bad error' warn 'Error' warn 'Error' end end ``` The following similar bits of code do not have the same problem: ```ruby # Before auto-correct unless error_list.nil? if error_list.first == 'Bad error' warn 'Error' warn 'Error' end end # After auto-correct (CORRECT) if !error_list.nil? && (error_list.first == 'Bad error') warn 'Error' warn 'Error' end ``` ```ruby # Before auto-correct if !error_list.nil? if error_list.first == 'Bad error' warn 'Error' end end # After auto-correct (CORRECT) warn 'Error' if !error_list.nil? && (error_list.first == 'Bad error') ``` -------- ## Expected behavior ` rubocop --auto-correct` should produce the following code: ```ruby if !error_list.nil? && (error_list.first == 'Bad error') warn 'Error' warn 'Error' end ``` ## Actual behavior Rubocop produces the following incorrect code. The code now throws an error if error_list is nil. ```ruby unless error_list.nil? && (error_list.first == 'Bad error') warn 'Error' warn 'Error' end ``` ## Steps to reproduce the problem Run `rubocop --auto-correct --debug code.rb` on the following code. ```ruby # frozen_string_literal: true error_list = nil if !error_list.nil? if error_list.first == 'Bad error' warn 'Error' warn 'Error' end end ``` Output on my machine: ``` For tmp: Default configuration from C:/Ruby27-x64/lib/ruby/gems/2.7.0/gems/rubocop-1.19.0/config/default.yml [Truncated] code.rb:6:3: C: [Corrected] Style/SoleNestedConditional: Consider merging nested conditions into outer if conditions. if error_list.first == 'Bad error' ^^ code.rb:7:5: C: [Corrected] Layout/IndentationConsistency: Inconsistent indentation detected. warn 'Error' ^^^^^^^^^^^^ code.rb:8:3: W: [Corrected] Layout/EndAlignment: end at 8, 2 is not aligned with unless at 5, 0. end ^^^ 1 file inspected, 5 offenses detected, 5 offenses corrected Finished in 0.658765800006222 seconds ``` ## RuboCop version ``` rubocop -V 1.19.0 (using Parser 3.0.2.0, rubocop-ast 1.10.0, running on ruby 2.7.4 x64-mingw32) ```
